dialogue.intro: You’re staring. Everyone does. If you’re here for a photo or an autograph, I’m off the clock. If you’re here to talk cards… then we can talk.
dialogue.repeat: Still hanging around? Most people lose interest once the bikini comes off. You must actually like the game.
talk: I've got a sunrise shoot tomorrow. Good money, terrible call time. If I can get one game in tonight, I'll survive.
People see the beach photos and assume I can't count prize cards. Sometimes it's useful to let them underestimate me.
My agent booked another lifestyle campaign. I asked her to leave me Saturday afternoon for the tournament. We negotiated.
I can hold a smile for three hours under a hot light. Somehow I still get nervous over a match I actually care about.
A photographer asked what I do for fun and laughed when I said cards. So I showed him how to play. He lost.
I keep a battered Trainer card from my first deck in my bag. It's in an ugly sleeve, and I'm not changing it.
dialogue.flirt: Careful. Most guys who flirt with me only want the version that exists in photos. You sure you’re different?
dialogue.duelWin: Huh. You actually made me work for it. That’s rarer than a first-edition holographic.
dialogue.duelLose: Okay, that one hurt. Rematch when I’m not still thinking about lighting setups.
hangouts: Sierra arrives at the arcade in a cover-up straight from a beach shoot. She pulls a deck list from her bag, points to three cards she wants to cut, and asks you to argue with her.
Between jobs, Sierra tests a disruption-heavy opening on her phone at the park. When you point out a weak turn, she makes you replay it until one of you changes their mind.
At the café she orders something strong, kicks off the heels she wore all day, and asks about your last match before you can ask about the photoshoot.
In the library, Sierra shows you her oldest Trainer card. The sleeve is scratched, the corner is bent, and she remembers the exact turn it won her first game.
After a close best-of-three, Sierra laughs at the move that beat her, writes it down on the back of a receipt, and insists you play again next weekend.

appearance.silhouette: Unambiguously adult 18-year-old, extremely slim and long-legged with a tiny chest and a disproportionately large, round, heavy ass. Narrow waist, flat stomach, model proportions that are intentionally bottom-heavy.
appearance.palette: Warm brunette, deep bronze skin tones, black, white, and coral/orange accents from her swimwear.
appearance.hair: Long, straight dark brunette hair usually worn loose or in a high sleek ponytail that swings past her waist.
appearance.eyes: Sharp hazel-green eyes that look bored or guarded until the topic turns to cards.
appearance.details: Minimal jewelry for shoots, a thin gold waist chain she often forgets to remove, a small deck box she carries everywhere, and a permanent slight model posture that softens when she’s comfortable.
appearance.expressions: Default cool/distant model face, rare genuine smile when talking strategy, focused competitive stare during matches, tired half-lidded look after long shoots, soft almost shy expression when someone actually listens to her about the game.
outfits: signature string bikini in coral or black (her actual job), often with a sheer open cover-up or oversized shirt thrown on afterward
tiny denim shorts that barely cover the bottom of her ass + cropped tank for casual days
tournament look: fitted black crop top, high-waisted shorts that still emphasize her hips and ass, sneakers
library/café: oversized hoodie that still can’t hide the silhouette, bike shorts
evening: simple slip dress that clings to her lower half and leaves almost nothing to the imagination from behind
appearance.renderNotes: SFW anime/JRPG style, age 18. Emphasize the extreme contrast: very slim upper body with tiny breasts and a large, round, heavy ass. She should look like a professional bikini model even in casual clothes. No nudity. When in swimwear keep it standard bikini (string or sport style). Match Neo Harbor’s clean, colorful aesthetic. Her body is deliberately fanservice-oriented but her face and posture should show she’s not performing for the player unless she’s working.
